title: perf: reuse synchronous content publication checks when retaining source bytes
body:
## Problem

The term-content cache rescans reservation indexes and published states immediately after the same synchronous call has validated and published a contiguous range. JMdict executes this work for its bounded recent-source cache.

## Change

Pass the successful contiguous-publication result directly into the cache step within the same synchronous call. This removes repeated published-state loads and a second contiguous-index scan. The proof is not stored and never crosses an await.

Source bounds, byte sums, average-size admission, backing-allocation accounting, cache capacity, eviction and ownership remain unchanged. Aliased reservation indexes retain the generic path. This builds on the merged immutable-source adoption change in #824.

## Validation

- 184 focused tests across two suites, including nine added semantic parity cases for owned/shared sources, partial coverage, cache budgets, eviction, identifier wrap, aliased indexes and short mapping tables.
- Main/test TypeScript and scoped ESLint pass.
- No new source allocations, cache state, production thresholds or persistence formats.

## Qualification

Frozen on develop `bbccabd520972cc351a65d9f545bd5369b6e9747`. Complete-import comparisons will determine whether this reduction is material; the cache's existing phase duration is only an upper bound on potential savings. Full source CI and browser qualification are pending. This remains a draft and no full-import speedup is claimed.

Original implementation; no third-party implementation code was copied.
